answer.answer: The goal was met: five settings on five different scenes failed on every repeat (S10, S4, S1, S13, S2). But none of the failures involved the pedestrian, so they don't answer the question about speed and step-out timing. The triage shows the same pattern in almost every run: the route command was RIGHT, and the policy went straight or drifted left. It then hit parked cars, oncoming traffic or a car in the next lane, or drove onto a median. The study never ran the nominal setting (1.0x, 0 s) on these scenes, so it can't say whether speed or timing matters here. They may fail anyway, which is the caveat the plan raised. Each confirmed case rests on only three or four runs, so its failure rate is known only to be somewhere above about half.

findings.claim: Five settings on five different scenes failed on every repeat: 18d28973 at 1.2x / +1.5 s, 0caa8f1a at 0.8x / +1 s, 048b974e at 1.4x / +1 s, 1bbe02fc at 1.4x / -0.5 s and 07981e6a at 1.4x / -1.5 s. A sixth scene, 0d4893f5 at 1.4x / -0.5 s, also failed on every repeat.

None of the triaged failures was a collision with the retimed pedestrian. The ego hit parked cars, oncoming cars or a car alongside it, rear-ended a lead car, or left the road. Most of these began with the policy ignoring a RIGHT route command and drifting left.

On 0caa8f1a, the ego crossed the double yellow line into the oncoming lanes and hit oncoming traffic head-on or side by side, at both 0.8x / +1 s and 1.4x / +1.5 s. The policy was at fault in every run. These runs are flagged as possible simulator artifacts only because the ego ended up over 3.5 m from the recorded path, and that drift is itself the failure.

On 18d28973 at 1.2x / +1.5 s, the ego stayed left when the route went right. It ran onto the grass median or rear-ended vehicle 99. The policy was at fault, and the artifact flags again reflect the drift from the recorded path.
On 048b974e and 07981e6a, the ego drove into cars parked along the left curb without braking. On 0d4893f5, it sideswiped a car in the adjacent left lane.

The 1bbe02fc case is weak. Its failures were off-road flags raised at the stop line while the ego was within half a metre of the recorded path. Triage judged one run not the policy's fault (a likely map or metric artifact) and the other two unclear.

The cleaner test scenes did not produce a confirmed failure. 18f8dbd6 never failed at 1.4x with 0 s or -1 s. 0e002edd never failed at 1.2x / -1.5 s. 0b10bce8 and 12a09194 had a single run each, with no failure. 0e002edd at 1.4x / +2 s failed once, by hitting a parked car, which is only a hint.

open: Is speed or timing actually behind these failures? Run the nominal 1.0x / 0 s setting about 3 times on each of 18d28973, 0caa8f1a, 048b974e, 1bbe02fc, 07981e6a and 0d4893f5. If they fail there too, the failure comes from the scene's route (missed right turn), not from the parameters.
Does the pedestrian's timing matter at all? On a failing scene, hold ego speed fixed and sweep actor_time_shift_s from -2 to +2 s. If nothing changes, the pedestrian plays no role.

Can the pedestrian be hit? The pedestrian conflict was never reached. Repeat the near misses on the cleaner scenes, 18f8dbd6 at 1.4x (-1 s, 0 s) and 0e002edd at 1.2x / -1.5 s, and report the closest approach to the pedestrian itself, not to any actor.
Is 1bbe02fc a real failure? Its off-road flags at the stop line may be a map or metric artifact, so it should be re-checked or replaced before it counts as a confirmed case.
Does the single failure on 0e002edd at 1.4x / +2 s repeat?
